extracted.intended_audience: African American authors and illustrators of children’s and young adult books; publishers and submitters to the Coretta Scott King Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and selection guidelines for the Coretta Scott King Book Awards: eligibility, selection criteria for writing and illustration, submission requirements, and related award-specific rules (John Steptoe New Talent; Virginia Hamilton Lifetime Achievement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award is given to an African American author and illustrator for outstanding inspirational and educational contributions. The Coretta Scott King Book Award titles promote understanding and appreciation of the culture of all peoples and their contribution to the realization of the American dream of a pluralistic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Award is also designed to commemorate the life and works of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and to honor Mrs. Coretta Scott King for her courage and determination to continue the work for peace and world brotherhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of the Black experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Must portray some aspect of the black experience, past, present, or future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrayal should be integral to the work and align with the Award's purpose to encourage artistic expression of the African American experience via literature and the graphic arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/illustrator identity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be written/illustrated by an African American.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core eligibility criterion for the Coretta Scott King Book Awards and associated categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Book must be published in the U.S. in the year preceding presentation of the Award, evidenced by the copyright date printed in the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example: only books published in 2023 will qualify for the 2024 award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of quality writing for youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Must meet established standards of quality writing for youth which include: clear plot; well drawn characters which portray growth and development during the course of the story; writing style which is consistent with and suitable to the age intended; accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sub-elements (clear plot, character development, age-appropriate style, accuracy) are used by the committee to assess the literary quality of submissions for youth readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience (age categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be written for a youth audience in one of three categories: Preschool–grade 4; Grades 5–8; Grades 9–12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should designate the intended age/grade range; the committee evaluates suitability of style and content for the stated age group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic/moral impact and reader motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular attention will be paid to titles which seek to motivate readers to develop their own attitudes and behaviors as well as comprehend their personal duty and responsibility as citizens in a pluralistic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that encourage civic understanding, responsibility, or development of moral attitudes consistent with pluralistic values are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration qualitative standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should reflect established qualitative standards: they should 'heighten and extend the readers' awareness of the world around him. They should lead him to an appreciation of beauty. The style and content of the illustrations should be...neither coy nor condescending...Storytelling qualities should enlarge upon the story elements that were hinted in the text and should include details that will awaken and strengthen the imagination of the reader and permit him to interpret the words and pictures in a manner unique to him' (Cianciolo, Illustrations in Children's Books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations are evaluated for how they enrich the text, extend storytelling, respect the reader, awaken imagination, and provide interpretive depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Author or illustrator must live in the U.S. or maintain dual residency/citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency or dual citizenship in the U.S. is required for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finished copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only finished copies will be accepted. Do not send advance reader copies, galleys, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must provide final, finished editions as evidence of publication; advance or prepublication materials are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-return and donation policy for submitted titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles submitted for the Coretta Scott King Book Awards will not be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles received by the ODLOS office are donated as part of The Coretta Scott King Books Awards Donation Grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital copy exception (supply chain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to supply chain issues throughout the publishing industry, digital copies of your book may be submitted if you are unable to submit a physical copy before the December 1st deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information or to use this exception, contact dponton@ala.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reviews or critiques from ALA/CSK Jury
rubrics_metrics.description: ALA Staff and the CSK Jury DOES NOT give reviews or critiques on books. This includes books being submitted to the Coretta Scott King Book Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should not expect feedback or editorial critique from award staff or jurors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories, honors, and winner benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards are given in author and illustrator categories; honor recipients may also be named. Both the Author and Illustrator Winner recipients receive a plaque and $1,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners are announced during the ALA Youth Media Awards Announcement (date varies by year). The CSK seal denotes winner/honor/Steptoe distinctions (bronze/silver/green respectively).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline and delivery instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be received by the jury by December 1, [year] at 11:59pm CST. Follow the mailing instructions in the confirmation to submit copies to the jury and ALA office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the current year's posted deadlines (e.g., all submissions must be received by the jury by December 1, 2025 at 11:59pm CST) and follow confirmation mailing instructions strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: John Steptoe Award for New Talent selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to affirm new talent and offer visibility to excellence in writing and/or illustration at the beginning of a career. Selection criteria: the criteria for eligibility will be the same as those for the writing and illustration awards, with the exception that the winner(s)' published works cannot exceed three in number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional rules: an author or illustrator who has already received or has just been selected to win one of the Coretta Scott King Book Awards in the current year is not eligible for the John Steptoe Award for New Talent. An author may receive this award one time. One award will be presented annually for text or illustrations; the committee may choose to select one book for writing and a second book for illustration. The award need not be given in a particular year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coretta Scott King – Virginia Hamilton Award for Lifetime Achievement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented in even years to an African American author, illustrator or author/illustrator for a body of published books for children and/or young adults who has made a significant and lasting literary contribution. In odd years, the award is presented to a practitioner for substantial contributions through active engagement with youth using award-winning African American literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients receive a medal and $1,500; the award alternates focus each year between creators (even years) and practitioners (odd years).
